summary: Darwin's Journey has players sending expedition teams around the Galapagos on a worker-placement/pick-up-and-deliver engine, fulfilling contracts, collecting species, and managing a ship route while a tense action-claiming mechanism forces tough ordering decisions. It's a rich, modern heavy euro with a strong sense of forward momentum and satisfying engine-building.
praised: Strong sense of progression and multiple viable strategies
criticised: Heavy rules overhead and long teach
Analysis paralysis potential with many simultaneous tracks
Some find the theme thin dressing over mechanisms
Long playtime for a full 4-player game

interaction.kind: claiming worker-placement spots and competing for the same contracts
interaction.detail: Players race to claim limited action spaces and fulfill overlapping contracts, so taking a spot or a contract first denies it to others, but each player otherwise advances their own exploration track and ship independently. The shared elements (action spaces, contract pool) are contested, while most of the engine-building happens on a private player board.
interaction.said: unknown — falling back on the mechanics of this Luciani-style worker-placement design

scoring.how_you_win: You place workers to gather goods and fulfill delivery contracts, which score points directly and advance you on tracks that pay out bonuses at game end; the highest total after the set number of eras/rounds wins.
